title: Introduce RAG Labbook: interactive scenario templates and offline eval runner
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: internal teams and community contributors asked for a small, composable set of local RAG scenarios that can be used for iterative prompt authoring, deterministic replay, and offline evaluation without requiring a full production index or cloud infra. This PR adds 'RAG Labbook' — a quickstart that packages scenario templates, a lightweight offline eval runner, telemetry probes, and a set of seeded corpora to reproduce common authoring workflows locally.

What this PR includes (summary): labbook README with quickstart and devloop; three scenario templates (cli-assistant, voice-assistant, and research-summarizer) that show tool-calling and structured outputs; an offline-eval runner that executes scenarios deterministically against seeded indices and records structured eval outputs; telemetry probe hooks and example probes configuration; a small CI smoke workflow and basic unit/flow tests.

Why it matters: teams can iterate on prompts, tool bindings, and structured-output validators against a reproducible dataset and measure regressions locally before pushing to hosted evals. The offline runner is intentionally minimal (single-process, deterministic seed control, and optional replay mode) so it can be used in CI and by contributors on laptops.

Usage notes (short): clone the quickstart, run docker-compose up to start the lightweight index and mock tool server, then run 'python offline-runner/run_eval.py --scenario=cli-assistant --seed=42 --output=results/cli-seed42.json'. The README contains step-by-step guides for authoring, invoking the local telemetry dashboard, and converting runner outputs into Redwood eval artifacts.

Checklist (all completed): - [x] Add scenario templates and sample prompts - [x] Implement offline-eval runner with deterministic seeds and replay option - [x] Add telemetry probe examples and toggles - [x] Provide CI smoketest that runs one scenario end-to-end - [x] Write README and quickstart guide with local troubleshooting tips - [x] Add unit tests for runner harness and template loader

Compatibility and limits: The quickstart targets Redwood SDK v0.22+ APIs and includes a compatibility shim for older local dev SDK versions. This is not intended for production indexing or benchmarking at scale; use it for authoring and small-scale validation only.

Related work: builds on ENG-4921 (authoring UX improvements) and complements the existing 'rag-authoring-playbook' content by offering an executable local harness that outputs structured eval artifacts ready for Redwood Optimize ingestion.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the offline-runner deterministic behavior, safety of the mock tool server (no external calls), and clarity of the README steps. CI run included e2e smoke. If accepted, I will follow up with a small package that converts runner outputs to the formal eval JSON schema (separate PR).

review_comments: Jonas Patel: Nice work — the deterministic seed behavior is exactly what the authoring team asked for. Two small asks: (1) please add a CLI flag to skip telemetry during CI runs; (2) include a short note in README about expected runtime on a dev laptop.
Maya Chen (author): Addressed both. Added --no-telemetry flag and noted typical runtimes in README (~30s for the example scenario with seed=42).
Leah Nguyen: CI looked flaky on first run (timeout on docker compose). Can we add a retry/wait strategy for the mock index service and a healthcheck?
Maya Chen (author): Added a healthcheck/wait loop in the CI smoke job and a more robust compose healthcheck for the index container. Reran CI — passing now.
Carlos Reyes: Suggest adding a small structured-output schema for the voice-assistant example so teams can test validators. Also OK to squash commits when merging.
Maya Chen (author): Added voice-assistant schema and example validator snippet in templates/README.
ci_notes: CI: one-time failure on docker startup due to race; fixed with healthcheck and re-run. All tests currently passing (unit + smoke).
release_notes: Add RAG Labbook quickstart: local scenario templates, deterministic offline eval runner, telemetry probes, and CI smoketests for prompt/tool authoring.
contribution_guidance: To extend scenarios add a YAML template to templates/ and a small prompt bundle in corpora/. Update run_eval.py to reference the new template name. Use --seed for deterministic runs and --replay to replay previous traces.
testing_instructions: Run tests: pytest quickstarts/rag-labbook/tests. To smoke-run: docker-compose -f quickstarts/rag-labbook/docker-compose.yml up --build; python quickstarts/rag-labbook/offline-runner/run_eval.py --scenario=research-summarizer --seed=101
notes_for_ops: Telemetry probes are disabled by default in CI via --no-telemetry. The mock tool server uses static stubs and does not make outbound network requests; still recommended to run behind a local firewall during security reviews.
risk_assessment: Low — this is a developer quickstart with no production traffic. The only infra is a local mock index and tool server. No secrets or production credentials are used.
